_note: Cases chosen by set difference between each model's feature_schema.json and WHO v2.1 (GARC1), not by intuition. Across the eight deployed bundles, 223 modelled mutations map to only 66 catalogue entries: 157 are absent from the catalogue entirely and 6 are graded U/F. Layer 2's remit is therefore most of what the models describe, and these cases exercise the boundary rather than sampling near it.

layer1-graded-resistant.why: rpoB@S450L is graded R by WHO v2.1. The catalogue must answer, and the RIF model must not run.

layer1-graded-across-drugs.why: katG@S315T is graded for INH but absent from the RIF catalogue while being a RIF model feature. One variant, two layers: the boundary is per drug, not per isolate.

layer2-catalogue-absent.why: rpoB@A692T is a RIF model feature that WHO v2.1 grades U. The model must fire AND must show its reasoning: this is the case the tool exists for. rpoB@D435Z is deliberately NOT used here despite being absent from the catalogue as a literal string -- piezo grades it R through the Z wildcard, which is how this case first failed. Literal set difference against the MUTATION column understates catalogue coverage; only piezo knows what the catalogue actually grades.

layer2-catalogue-ungraded.why: inhA@I21T and inhA@I194T are graded U by WHO v2.1 -- present but of uncertain significance. U is not a call, so the model answers. This is the case the paper's framing names explicitly.

layer2-no-variants.why: Nothing carried. The catalogue grades nothing, the model answers from the intercept, and the reliability band must be capped for want of evidence.

mixed-isolate.why: A realistic MDR isolate: RIF and INH graded by the catalogue, EMB left to the model. A single report must carry rows from both layers and label each.
